# 美債自盤中高殖利率回穩，科技股卻明顯下挫

## 長債買盤回流，通膨補償仍上升

美債早盤隨全球債市續跌，隨後收復失土。10年期殖利率一度接近4.75%、創19個月高點，30年期約在5.32%至5.33%、為2007年以來最高。紐約收盤時，10年期反而下跌1個基點至4.71%，30年期跌3個基點至5.28%；5年期跌1個基點至4.37%，2年期維持4.19%。曲線小幅趨平，2年與10年期利差為52個基點，2年與30年期為109個基點。

舒緩來自實質殖利率。10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.41%，抵銷損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點至2.30%的影響。美伊僵局持續，布蘭特仍高於$91。買方願意在較高殖利率承接長債，卻未認定能源風險已結束；10年與30年期殖利率近一個月仍分別高16及22個基點。

科技股並未跟著回穩。半導體下跌4.98%，Nasdaq 100跌1.68%，S&P 500跌0.69%。VIX上升4.28%至15.84，水準仍低，美元則大致持平。這更像集中在長期折現率與融資需求的敏感度，而非全面搶進美元資金。

信用市場繼續滿足融資需求，但利率不低。QTS的5年期投資級專案債雖有最高$230億訂單，$39億發行仍以7.228%定價。德國€40億30年期債也獲大量需求，借款殖利率卻創15年高點。日本5年期標售找到買家，超長端殖利率仍上升。各市場的需求取決於年期、結構與價格，不只是手上有沒有現金。

## 活動數據支持等待，尚非降息共識

7月工業生產增加0.2%，低於預期0.3%，6月卻由0.1%上修至0.3%。當期較弱，前期比原先強；搭配近期就業、通膨及零售報告，這支持Fed等待而非立即升息，尚不足以證明產出大幅惡化。

選擇權交易開始增加對未來政策轉向的保護。買方出現在押注9月維持利率的組合，以及受惠於預期利率下降的2027年3月、6月買權。部分投資人平倉原先押注高利率的9月及12月賣權。交換市場仍反映9月緊縮9個基點、至2027年6月約40個基點。對降息避險不等於降息已成主要預測，長債選擇權也仍為進一步下跌收取保護溢價。

油價讓耐心仍有條件。川普稱美伊沒有正在進行或排定的談判，卻也形容荷莫茲已開放運作；6月備忘錄到期後，航運證據並未支持迅速正常化。阿聯表示，兩枚朝該國發射的伊朗彈道飛彈落海。戰前全球五分之一石油及LNG經過荷莫茲。

布蘭特上漲0.58%至$91.40，WTI則近乎持平於$84.52。2年期不動、實質殖利率下降，顯示投資人未將每次油價上升都直接轉成下一場Fed會議的升息；通膨補償增加，仍保留供應問題未解的保障。

科技股跌勢使整體氣氛沒有美債收盤看來那麼輕鬆。AI曝險已橫跨股票、公司債、資料中心債、租約支持載體與銀行融資。長期殖利率升高，同時影響遠期獲利價值，以及創造獲利所需的資金成本。黃金期貨下跌0.71%至$4,386.50，高利率提高持有無孳息資產的機會成本。尾盤債券買盤減輕了一項壓力，沒有抹去更廣泛的重新定價。

## 德國借款更貴，法國與日本另有財政限制

德國透過承銷團發行€40億、2056年8月到期債券，殖利率3.783%，為2011年以來最高30年期融資成本。訂單超過€380億，供給順利消化，但價格高於7月較小規模一般標售的3.64%。

2027年預算草案顯示€2,040億淨融資需求。德國商業銀行Hauke Siemssen估計，明年Bund淨發行€1,630億，高於2026年的約€1,370億；到期€2,380億之下，總發行約€4,000億。國庫券、現金、資產出售及KfW款項，可降低須透過Bund籌措的金額，國防與基建計畫卻仍增加借款。承銷拓展買家，不會改變根本需求。

法國則在全球走勢之外，多了政治風險。2027年預算攻防與4月總統選舉之前，空頭部位增加，主力10年期債期貨未平倉量升至6月初以來最高。總理Sebastien Lecornu在分裂國會中爭取赤字低於5%，並警告若無共識，計畫可能拖到明年、赤字達6.5%。30年期殖利率接近4.90%、創2008年以來最高，10年期對德國利差85個基點、為10月以來最寬。

Natixis的Theophile Legrand估計，法國自身風險約貢獻25個基點，為2025年12月預算緊張以來最多。財長Roland Lescure將2026年成長預測由0.9%下修至0.7%，並稱赤字由2025年5.1%降至5%的目標有難度。火災、高溫及乾旱增加紓困需求，Lecornu卻抗拒增稅。去年秋季惠譽、標普及Morningstar DBRS降評、穆迪調低展望後，惠譽8月28日評估將展開新一輪檢視；這是未來評估，不是已經再次降評。

ECB首席經濟學家Philip Lane預期，通膨至年底約3%，取決於伊朗衝突，仍高於2%目標。7月通膨2.9%，第二季成長0.4%、優於預期。他未承諾6月升息25個基點後再升，但強調不能讓過高通膨持續，並指出明年夏季的天候食品風險。新增供給到來時，貨幣政策未提供明確抵銷。

日本需求落在曲線中段，而非超長端。5年期標售投標倍數4.15，高於前次3.43及12個月平均3.34；尾差由0.03降至0.02，5年期殖利率跌1.5個基點至2.145%。不過，76%配售給未具名投標者，這部分需求會持有多久尚不清楚。

20年期殖利率上升4個基點至3.85%，30年期升5個基點至4.125%。政府兩年食品稅減免的財源未明，BOJ卻在進口通膨與弱日圓之下減少購債。協助管理瑞穗JPY41兆證券部位的Kenya Koshimizu表示，銀行避開抗通膨債與一年內年期以外的日債。他認為9月升息機率高，也不排除年底前兩次升息、將利率由1%帶至1.5%。這是投資人判斷，不是BOJ指引，但說明5年期強勁結果背後仍有戒心。

## QTS以7.228%完成發行，Alphabet提供新市場溢價

QTS旗下QualityTech的兩家特殊目的子公司，為喬治亞州Project Odyssey發行$39億5年期票據。資金將用於微軟相關資料中心的施工、開發、營運、一般公司支出，以及對QualityTech的分配。交易比初始討論大約增加$10億，需求高峰最高$230億、約發行六倍，今年投資級平均約四倍。

行銷過程中殖利率收窄40個基點，最終仍達7.228%。穆迪評等Baa3、惠譽BBB-，皆為最低投資級，且兩年內不可買回。微軟關係有助收入基礎，卻不會使專案債等同微軟自身負債；投資人仍承擔施工、集中及剩餘資產價值風險。

舊券呈現這些風險如何交易。QTS子公司4月$46億10年期發行，原殖利率5.7%，週二已約7.16%，接近B級水準；上週另一筆Zenith Arc $22.5億發行也轉弱。重複供給及仰賴少數AI租戶，可能讓報酬與單看投資級標籤的想像大不相同。

Alphabet首次澳幣債仍在行銷，四個年期目標約A$50億、或$36億。3年期初始指引約較本地基準高80個基點，相較類似美元債換成澳幣後約56個基點；其他年期最初較換匯後同類券高約20至25個基點。這些是可能隨訂單而收窄的初步讓利，不是已完成的借款成本。

公司已在美元、瑞郎、英鎊、歐元、加幣及日圓市場借款，2026年資本支出預測提高至最高$2,050億。評等分析師警告，超大型雲端業者債務增速高於收入，使變現能力與投入資本報酬更重要。摩根資產管理Gabriela Santos估計，公私市場AI資本支出達$5.5兆，並強調債券與股票曝險重疊。同一套融資循環，可能透過多個工具同時存在於投資組合。

私人交易也擴大。服務軍方及商業客戶的波音、洛克希德馬丁合資United Launch Alliance，將私人債券融資由$5億增至$15億，四個年期介於3年至10年。Ripple Prime發行$2.75億2031年到期優先無擔保票據，票息8.25%、KBRA評等BBB，隨美國主經紀商業務擴張，用於一般公司用途。私人發行可避開波動的公開簿冊，仍讓機構貸款人以不低票息承諾資金。

8月投資級供給截至週一已超過$1,450億，當日12家發行人新增$91億。公司及主權風險不同，卻共同占用長期資金。QTS結果與美債回穩，都顯示買方會回應價格，只是專案信用需要更高補償與更明確結構保障。廣泛基金仍平穩：LQD上漲0.13%，HYG與JNK則分別跌約0.10%及0.11%。

## 本地政策支持中國與印尼，印度調整融資組合

中國30年期公債殖利率降至2.15%，為11月底以來最低；10年與30年期利差收至約50個基點，接近2月以來最窄，30年期債期貨未平倉量則在週五創紀錄。7月產出、消費與投資疲弱，增強寬鬆及持續低迷的預期，提供本地買進長債的理由。

Shanze Fund的Song Xiaofei將漲勢主要歸因於短期交易部位，而非持久機構配置。曲線轉平壓縮銀行利潤，與海外利差劣勢擴大也可能增加資金外流及人民幣壓力。地方政府發行在上半年落後後，第三季預計創紀錄。Song認為，利差若要低於40個基點，需要供給減慢與長線買家加入。這是本地成長及流動性的行情，不是全球通膨風險消失。

印度外幣存款優惠已吸引逾$500億，提前結束卻降低未來盧比流動性。花旗將流入預測下修$100億至$700億，野村則由最高$900億降至約$720億。銀行將不少資金配置於4年至5年期公債，窗口縮短便限制熱門陡峭化交易的空間，也增加近期再融資壓力。

另一境外借款方案仍開放至12月，對平均到期至少三年提供固定年率1.5%的換匯。ICICI週一$7.5億發行，讓印度金融機構今年美元發行達$88.5億，超過2019年$79.2億紀錄。Kotak Mahindra準備5年期債，Yes Bank已聘顧問。強勁簿冊支持收窄定價，普通避險成本恢復前可能先加速發行，之後再降溫。

印尼財政承諾繼續支持資產。週二股市上漲0.8%，自6月低點回升約21%，5年期殖利率跌4個基點至6月18日以來最低，10年期兩週已跌16個基點。2027年赤字目標2.4%、低於3%法定上限，且未加另一大型支出方案，配合央行延續性信心，改善市場情緒。

執行仍待觀察。美銀估計，明年總發行可能仍接近$440億，也可能包含未列入表面赤字的支出。Prabowo追求2026年及2027年各6%成長，政府過去曾一面調高保守赤字，一面將資源轉向免費餐食。較務實的匯率、通膨及融資假設降低即時不確定性，收入與支出約束仍須實現，才能支持債市改善。

韓國的政策價格則有爭議。一年期隱含利率3.79%，遠高於政策利率2.75%，即使7月通膨降至2.8%、低於預期。M&G的Low Guan Yi只預期再升25個基點，而非市場約100個基點。晶片景氣使上半年公司稅收入增9.6%至KRW49.3兆，這位經理人認為追加支出可因此不增加債券供給。不過，外資7月賣出約$12億公債，10年期殖利率自6月升22個基點，判斷仍面對部位與油價風險。

烏拉圭則連續第四次維持5.75%。7月通膨升至4.3%，仍低於4.5%目標，受訪機構預期10月才升息25個基點。主權長債整體環境困難，本地通膨及財政空間仍能區分政策路徑。

## Sammons回應審視，Avison Young以債轉股降低負擔

Sammons Financial的2036年6月債利差進一步升至約240個基點，一週前147個基點。該筆$7.5億10年期發行後兩週，公司又發行$5億5年期債。與Mark Walter旗下Guggenheim業務的關係持續受到審視，利差也再度擴大。

Hunterbrook Media的投資關係企業已揭露空頭，報導引用文件仍將Sammons稱為關係人，並承認可能有偏向其利益的誘因。Sammons回應，母公司Sammons Enterprises在Guggenheim Capital僅有無投票權、非控制性持分，且多年來一直減少。公司稱母公司不持有投票權或普通股，無法控制Guggenheim Capital、TWG Global Holdings或關係企業，其主管、董事及員工也未受調查。

否認控制權之外，經濟聯繫仍重要。Guggenheim替保險公司管理數百億美元，長期將Sammons視為最大股東；檢察官與監管單位正在調查Walter相關保險公司，向其商業版圖其他部分提供的貸款。Guggenheim 2031年11月第一順位貸款週一低於面額80%，7月20日約面額；惠譽對Sammons的A-評估則提及資本極強、風險資產略高。市場價格與具有利益關係的報導都不等於不當行為獲證實，投資人正提高對關係人經濟利益如何影響資產配置的重視。

Avison Young則以債權人持股改善償債。資本重整將債務換股，年度現金利息降低逾70%，槓桿降至EBITDA三倍以下。執行長Mark Rose預期10月完成，並稱貸款人會加注股本，支持招聘及併購，包括資料中心與辦公室轉型。這家加拿大房地產顧問公司的合夥人，完成後約保留一半持股。方案透過讓貸款人成為股東取得營運彈性，回收更直接取決於商業地產與執行，而非另一次再融資。

## Fed溝通與接下來的長期資金承諾

8月19日7月FOMC會議紀錄與Warsh下週傑克森洞發言，將釐清對就業、通膨及零售轉弱的反應。耐心觀察的說法，符合週二2年期不動、通膨補償升而實質殖利率降的組合；若更擔心油價轉嫁或緊縮不足，短端可能重新加入通膨定價。

日本8月20日20年期標售接在強勁5年期之後，但起點殖利率3.85%，超長端買方仍謹慎。它將顯示中段需求是否願意延伸到更長的財政與政策曝險，政府食品稅財源也仍未定。

美國方面，華盛頓都會機場管理局8月19日將表決增加$155億資本預算，主要以$142億債券支應。五項工程總計$199億，其中$44億已授權。通過代表建立大型未來市政融資方案，不是立即出售全部債券。

荷莫茲實際船流、運費與保險成本，仍比口頭宣布重啟重要。恢復通行及油價下降，可減輕使布蘭特維持$91.40的壓力，並擴大債券舒緩；僵局與攻擊持續，則增加能源進入實際通膨及政策的風險。2年期殖利率與通膨補償同步上升，將標誌這項改變；若再由長端實質殖利率主導轉陡，供給與AI融資仍較關鍵。

overall_summary.headline: 美債自盤中高殖利率回穩，科技股卻明顯下挫
overall_summary.session_narrative:
30年期殖利率一度約5.32%至5.33%，收盤反跌3個基點至5.28%。10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點，通膨補償升2個基點。工業生產略遜預期，但6月上修減輕疲弱訊號。

半導體下跌4.98%，Nasdaq 100跌1.68%，美元穩定與低水準VIX未顯示全面搶資金。QTS以最高$230億訂單支持$39億發行，結構仍要求7.228%殖利率。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Treasuries recover from intraday highs as technology shares fall

## Long-bond buyers return, but inflation compensation rises

Treasuries recovered after an early extension of the global bond selloff. Ten-year yields reached about 4.75%, a 19-month high, and the 30-year traded around 5.32%–5.33%, its highest since 2007. By the New York close, the ten-year was down 1 basis point at 4.71% and the 30-year down 3 at 5.28%. Five-year yields eased 1 to 4.37%, while the two-year stayed at 4.19%. The curve flattened slightly, with 2s10s at 52 basis points and 2s30s at 109.

Real yields supplied the relief. The ten-year real yield fell 3 basis points to 2.41%, outweighing a 2-basis-point rise in breakevens to 2.30%. Brent remained above $91 as the US-Iran impasse continued. Buyers accepted long debt at the higher yields, but had not decided the energy risk was over: ten- and 30-year yields remained 16 and 22 basis points higher over a month.

The recovery did not extend to technology shares. Semiconductors fell 4.98%, Nasdaq 100 lost 1.68% and the S&P 500 declined 0.69%. VIX rose 4.28% to 15.84, still restrained, and the dollar was little changed. The selloff exposed concentrated sensitivity to long discount rates and financing needs rather than a broad rush for dollar funding.

Credit markets continued to supply those needs at substantial yields. QTS priced $3.9 billion of five-year investment-grade project debt at 7.228%, despite peak orders of as much as $23 billion. Germany's €4 billion 30-year sale also drew strong demand at its highest borrowing yield in 15 years. Japan's five-year auction found buyers while superlong yields rose. Across markets, demand depended on maturity, structure and price, not simply the availability of cash.

## Softer activity encourages patience, not a new consensus for cuts

July industrial production rose 0.2%, below the 0.3% forecast, but June was revised to 0.3% from 0.1%. A softer current reading therefore followed stronger history. Alongside the recent labor, inflation and retail reports, it supported waiting at the Fed rather than an immediate increase; it did not establish a sharp deterioration in output.

Options trading began to reflect more protection against an eventual policy pivot. Buyers appeared in September structures aimed at a hold and in March and June 2027 calls benefiting from lower expected rates. Some traders unwound September and December puts used for higher-rate outcomes. Swaps nevertheless still priced 9 basis points of September tightening and about 40 by June 2027. Hedges against cuts are not the same as cuts becoming the central forecast, and long-bond options retained a premium for further downside protection.

Oil kept the case for patience conditional. Trump said no talks with Iran were occurring or scheduled, even while describing Hormuz as open and operating. Shipping evidence did not establish rapid normalization after the June memorandum expired. The UAE reported two Iranian ballistic missiles falling into the sea after being fired toward the country. Before the war, a fifth of global oil and LNG had passed through Hormuz.

Brent gained 0.58% to $91.40, while WTI was almost unchanged at $84.52. The stable two-year yield and lower real yields showed that investors were not translating every oil increase directly into the next Fed decision. Higher breakevens still preserved compensation for unresolved supply risk.

Technology's losses made the session less comfortable than the Treasury close alone suggests. AI exposure now spans equities, corporate bonds, data-center debt, lease-backed vehicles and bank facilities. Higher long yields affect both the value of distant earnings and the financing used to produce them. Gold futures fell 0.71% to $4,386.50 as high yields increased the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. Late bond buying eased one pressure without undoing the broader repricing.

## Germany pays more; France and Japan face separate fiscal constraints

Germany sold €4 billion maturing in August 2056 through a syndicate at 3.783%, its highest 30-year borrowing yield since 2011. Orders exceeded €38 billion. The government placed the debt comfortably, but paid more than the 3.64% yield at July's smaller conventional auction.

The 2027 draft budget points to a €204 billion net financing requirement. Commerzbank's Hauke Siemssen estimates net Bund issuance of €163 billion next year, up from about €137 billion in 2026, with gross sales around €400 billion and €238 billion maturing. Bills, cash, asset sales and KfW payments could reduce the amount funded through Bunds, but defense and infrastructure plans still add borrowing. Syndication broadens the buyer base without changing that underlying requirement.

French yields added political risk to the global move. Active ten-year futures open interest reached its highest since early June as bearish positions built ahead of the 2027 budget fight and April presidential election. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu seeks a deficit below 5% in a divided parliament; he warned that failure to agree could push a plan into next year and leave the deficit as high as 6.5%. The 30-year yield approached 4.90%, its highest since 2008, and the ten-year spread over Germany reached 85 basis points, widest since October.

Natixis's Theophile Legrand attributes about 25 basis points to France-specific risk, the most since December 2025 budget tensions. Finance Minister Roland Lescure cut the 2026 growth forecast from 0.9% to 0.7% and called a 5% deficit target, versus 5.1% in 2025, difficult. Lecornu has resisted tax increases as fires, heat and drought add support demands. Fitch's August 28 review begins another rating sequence after last autumn's Fitch, S&P and Morningstar DBRS downgrades and Moody's outlook reduction. The review is upcoming, not a further downgrade already delivered.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane expects inflation around 3% through year-end, depending on the Iran conflict, against the 2% target. July inflation was 2.9% and second-quarter growth a stronger-than-expected 0.4%. He did not commit to another hike after June's quarter-point increase, but stressed the need to prevent prolonged excessive inflation and flagged weather-related food risks next summer. Higher issuance is arriving without a clear monetary-policy offset.

Japan found demand in the belly rather than the superlong sector. The five-year auction's 4.15 bid-to-cover exceeded the previous 3.43 and 12-month average of 3.34. Its tail narrowed from 0.03 to 0.02, and the five-year yield fell 1.5 basis points to 2.145%. Unidentified bidders received 76% of the sale, however, leaving the holding horizon of much of that demand uncertain.

The 20-year yield rose 4 basis points to 3.85% and the 30-year 5 to 4.125%. Financing for the government's two-year food-tax reduction remains unexplained, while the BOJ is reducing purchases and facing imported inflation and yen weakness. Mizuho's Kenya Koshimizu, who helps oversee a JPY41 trillion securities portfolio, said the bank avoids JGBs outside inflation-linked debt and maturities within a year. He sees a high chance of a September hike and would not rule out two by year-end, taking the policy rate from 1% to 1.5%. That is an investor's assessment, not BOJ guidance, but it illustrates the caution behind the strong five-year result.

## QTS completes its sale at 7.228%; Alphabet offers a new-market concession

Two special-purpose subsidiaries of QTS unit QualityTech issued $3.9 billion of five-year notes for Project Odyssey in Georgia. Proceeds fund construction, development and operation of the Microsoft-linked data center, general corporate expenses and distributions to QualityTech. The transaction grew by roughly $1 billion from initial discussions. Peak demand reached as much as $23 billion, about six times the issue compared with roughly four times on average in high grade this year.

The yield tightened 40 basis points during marketing but still finished at 7.228%. Moody's rated the notes Baa3 and Fitch BBB-, the lowest investment-grade tiers; they cannot be called for two years. The Microsoft relationship supports the revenue proposition without making project debt equivalent to Microsoft's own obligations. Investors still bear construction, concentration and residual-asset exposure.

Older bonds show how those risks can trade. QTS subsidiaries' $4.6 billion ten-year issue from April, originally yielding 5.7%, traded around 7.16% Tuesday, close to single-B levels. The separate $2.25 billion Zenith Arc issue from last week also weakened. Repeated issuance and reliance on a small set of AI tenants can produce materially different returns from what the investment-grade label alone might suggest.

Alphabet's debut Australian-dollar deal remained in marketing, targeting about A$5 billion, or $3.6 billion, in four maturities. Initial three-year guidance was near 80 basis points over the local benchmark, versus about 56 on comparable dollar debt swapped into Australian dollars. Other tranches initially offered roughly 20–25 basis points over swapped equivalents. Those are preliminary concessions that may tighten with orders, not completed borrowing costs.

The company has already borrowed in dollars, Swiss francs, sterling, euros, Canadian dollars and yen, and raised its 2026 capex forecast to as much as $205 billion. Rating analysts warn that hyperscaler debt is rising faster than revenue, making monetization and returns on invested capital increasingly important. JPMorgan Asset Management's Gabriela Santos estimated AI capex across public and private markets at $5.5 trillion and stressed the overlap between bond and equity exposure. Portfolios can hold the same financing cycle through several instruments.

Private deals also expanded. United Launch Alliance, the Boeing–Lockheed Martin venture serving military and commercial customers, increased a private-bond financing from $500 million to $1.5 billion across four tranches from three to ten years. Ripple Prime raised $275 million of senior unsecured notes due in 2031 at an 8.25% coupon, rated BBB by KBRA, for general corporate uses as its US prime-brokerage business expands. Private execution can avoid a volatile public book, but still commits institutional lenders at substantial coupons.

August high-grade supply had already exceeded $145 billion by Monday, when 12 issuers added $9.1 billion. Corporate and sovereign risks differ, but both draw on duration capacity. QTS's result and the Treasury recovery each show buyers responding to price, with much greater compensation and explicit structural protection required in project credit. Broad funds remained orderly: LQD gained 0.13%, while HYG and JNK fell about 0.10% and 0.11%, respectively.

## Local policy supports China and Indonesia, while India adjusts its funding mix

China's 30-year government yield fell to 2.15%, its lowest since late November. The 10s30s spread narrowed toward 50 basis points, near its smallest since February, after 30-year futures open interest reached a record Friday. Weak July output, consumption and investment strengthened expectations of easing and sustained softness, creating a domestic reason to buy duration.

Shanze Fund's Song Xiaofei attributed the rally mainly to short-term portfolios rather than durable institutional allocations. A flatter curve reduces bank margins, and a larger yield disadvantage overseas can add capital-outflow and yuan pressure. Local-government issuance is expected to reach a third-quarter record after lagging in the first half. Song said a spread below 40 basis points would require slower supply and longer-horizon buyers. The rally reflects local growth and liquidity, not a global disappearance of inflation risk.

India's early end to its foreign-currency deposit incentive reduced expected rupee liquidity after attracting more than $50 billion. Citigroup lowered its inflow estimate by $10 billion to $70 billion; Nomura cut its estimate from as much as $90 billion to about $72 billion. Banks had deployed much of the liquidity in four- to five-year government bonds, so the shorter window curtailed a popular steepener and increased near-term refinancing pressure.

A separate offshore-borrowing facility remains open through December, with a fixed annual swap rate of 1.5% for average maturity of at least three years. ICICI's $750 million Monday sale took Indian financial-institution dollar issuance to $8.85 billion this year, above 2019's $7.92 billion record. Kotak Mahindra was preparing five-year debt and Yes Bank had appointed advisers. Strong books have supported tighter pricing; the calendar may accelerate before ordinary hedging costs return and slow the activity.

Indonesia's fiscal promise continued to help assets. Equities gained 0.8% Tuesday, bringing the recovery from June lows to about 21%, and five-year yields fell 4 basis points to their lowest since June 18. Ten-year yields had declined 16 basis points in two weeks. The 2027 deficit target of 2.4%, within the legal 3% ceiling and without another major spending program, worked alongside greater confidence in central-bank continuity.

Execution remains unresolved. Bank of America estimates total issuance could still approach $44 billion next year, potentially including spending below the headline deficit. Prabowo seeks 6% growth in both 2026 and 2027, and his administration has previously raised a conservative deficit while reallocating resources to free meals. Realistic currency, inflation and funding assumptions reduced immediate uncertainty; revenue delivery and restraint must now substantiate the bond-market improvement.

Korea presents a disputed policy price. Its one-year implied rate was 3.79%, well above the 2.75% policy rate, despite July inflation slowing more than expected to 2.8%. M&G's Low Guan Yi expects only another 25 basis points, not the roughly 100 priced. First-half corporate tax revenue rose 9.6% to KRW49.3 trillion with the chip boom, which the manager sees as room for supplementary spending without more bond supply. Foreigners sold about $1.2 billion of government debt in July and ten-year yields were up 22 basis points since June, leaving the view exposed to positioning and oil.

Uruguay instead held at 5.75% for a fourth meeting. July inflation rose to 4.3% but remained below the 4.5% target, and surveyed institutions expect a quarter-point increase only in October. Local inflation and fiscal capacity continue to distinguish policy paths even within a generally difficult market for sovereign duration.

## Sammons responds to scrutiny; Avison Young exchanges debt for equity

Sammons Financial's June 2036 spread widened further to about 240 basis points, from 147 a week earlier. The $750 million ten-year issue was followed two weeks later by $500 million of five-year notes. The further widening came as scrutiny continued over ties to Mark Walter's Guggenheim businesses.

Hunterbrook Media, whose investment affiliate disclosed a short position, cited filings that continued to call Sammons a related party and acknowledged incentives to favor it. Sammons responded that parent Sammons Enterprises has only a non-voting, non-controlling interest in Guggenheim Capital, reduced over several years. It said the parent has no voting or common equity and no ability to control Guggenheim Capital, TWG Global Holdings or affiliates, and that its officers, directors and employees are not under investigation.

Economic links remain relevant alongside that denial of control. Guggenheim managed tens of billions for the insurer and had long regarded Sammons as its largest shareholder. Prosecutors and regulators are examining Walter-linked insurer loans directed to other parts of his business empire. The November 2031 Guggenheim first-lien loan was below 80 cents Monday, from around par July 20, while Fitch's A- assessment of Sammons cited very strong capital but somewhat elevated risky assets. Neither market prices nor an interested report establish wrongdoing; investors are assigning more weight to how related-party economics affect asset allocation.

Avison Young is using creditor ownership to improve debt service. Its recapitalization swaps debt for equity, cuts annual cash interest by more than 70% and brings leverage below three times EBITDA. CEO Mark Rose expects an October closing and said lenders will add equity for hiring and acquisitions, including data centers and office conversions. Partners would retain roughly half the Canadian property adviser's ownership. The plan gives operating flexibility by making lenders owners, leaving recovery more directly dependent on commercial property and execution rather than another refinancing.

## Fed communication and upcoming duration commitments

July FOMC minutes on August 19 and Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks next week will clarify the response to softer employment, inflation and retail demand. A patient account would be consistent with Tuesday's unchanged two-year yield and lower real yields despite higher breakevens. Greater concern about oil pass-through or insufficient restraint could bring the front end back into inflation repricing.

Japan's August 20 twenty-year auction follows the strong five-year result, but starts with a 3.85% yield and cautious superlong buyers. It will show whether belly demand extends to longer fiscal and policy exposure. The government's food-tax financing remains unsettled.

In the US, the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority votes August 19 on adding $15.5 billion to its capital budget, mainly financed by $14.2 billion of bonds. Five construction packages cost $19.9 billion, with $4.4 billion already authorized. Approval would establish a large future municipal funding program, not an immediate sale of all the debt.

Actual Hormuz traffic, freight and insurance costs remain more important than descriptions of reopening. Restoration and lower crude would reduce the pressure keeping Brent at $91.40 and could broaden bond relief. Continued deadlock or attacks would increase the risk of energy entering realized inflation and policy. Joint increases in two-year yields and breakevens would mark that change; renewed steepening led by long real yields would leave supply and AI financing more central.
